title: The quadratic growth of Krylov spread complexity in the BTZ black hole
authors: Aranya Bhattacharya, Mario Flory, Michal P. Heller, Emiliano Rizza, Tim Schuhmann
abstract: The boundary quantity that captures the growth of black-hole interiors quantified by holographic complexity remains unknown beyond 2d dilaton gravity. We provide a critical analysis of a partition-function construction of Krylov spread complexity for thermofield-double states that provides a dimension-independent boundary reconstruction from semiclassical holographic partition functions, while developing the present dynamical and bulk construction for the BTZ saddle. In the double-scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model, where exact and semiclassical results can be compared, we show that the classical limit is reliable only when taken after the complexity has been reconstructed; taking this limit at the level of individual Lanczos coefficients discards essential information. Applying the construction to a large-central-charge two-dimensional conformal field theory above the Hawking-Page temperature dual to a Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli black hole, we find an intermediate departure from early-time quadratic growth followed by behavior compatible with a return toward asymptotically quadratic growth, rather than the linear late-time behavior of the volume and the standard finite-functional complexity = anything class. We then match this boundary behavior to a generalized complexity = anything bulk object built from an infinite series of extrinsic-curvature invariants. The construction provides a systematic route from black-hole thermodynamics to Krylov dynamics and can naturally be extended to higher-dimensional holographic black holes.
summary: This paper develops a systematic method using Krylov spread complexity to probe black hole interiors holographically. By analyzing the BTZ black hole dual to a 2D CFT, the authors show that the complexity exhibits quadratic late-time growth ($\gamma=2$), which requires careful resummation of infinite series invariants. This work provides a powerful new tool linking quantum dynamics (Krylov theory) directly to gravitational thermodynamics.
main_problem: The primary challenge is determining a robust boundary quantity that accurately captures the growth of black-hole interiors quantified by holographic complexity, especially beyond simple 2D gravity models.
main_result: The authors establish that for the BTZ black hole dual to CFT2, Krylov spread complexity exhibits an intermediate departure from early-time quadratic growth, followed by behavior compatible with asymptotically quadratic growth ($\gamma=2$).
method: The work employs a combination of holographic duality (relating bulk geometry to boundary quantum dynamics), the moment method applied to Lanczos recursion for Krylov spread complexity, and advanced asymptotic analysis techniques like Padé continuation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on black holes, specifically the BTZ black hole in 2D, which is dual to a large-central-charge two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT). A benchmark system used for comparison is the double-scaled Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev (DSSYK) model.
key_observables: Krylov spread complexity ($C_K(t)$), generalized complexity built from extrinsic-curvature invariants, and the asymptotic growth rate ($\gamma$) of this complexity.
important_parameters: The analysis examines different time/temperature regimes (early vs. late times) and requires careful handling of the order in which semiclassical limits are taken relative to the reconstruction of the complexity measure.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include the validity of holographic duality for these systems and the necessity of resumming infinite series expansions (like those involving extrinsic-curvature invariants) to capture the correct asymptotic behavior.
figures_summary: The notes describe a comparison between finite truncations of an expansion (showing linear growth, $\gamma=1$) and the fully resummed function (showing quadratic growth, $\gamma=2$), illustrating the non-commutativity of limits.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the theoretical gap in complexity measures, then using the DSSYK model as a controlled benchmark to establish an 'order-of-limits' rule. It then applies this framework to the BTZ black hole/CFT2 system, deriving and analyzing the resulting asymptotic behavior of $C_K(t)$ through detailed mathematical expansions.
why_interesting: This work connects concepts from quantum information (complexity measures), general relativity (black holes/BTZ geometry), and advanced mathematical physics (spectral theory via Krylov methods). The focus on non-trivial asymptotic scaling ($\gamma=2$ vs $\gamma=1$) is highly relevant to understanding the deep structure of holographic entanglement and complexity.

All data are for q = 0.95. In both coefficients, an emergent linear regime at intermediate n is visible for nonzero β.

We see rapid conver- gence of the Pad´e approximation towards the exact answer.

Comparison of Lanczos coefficients a0(β) and b1(β) (normalized by appropriate powers of |log q|) from numerics at various temperatures β(θ) (dots) with analytical predictions a(sc) 0 (β) and b(sc) 1 (β) (blue dashed) from the semiclassical par- tition function of DSSYK via CfZ. All data are for q = 0.95. The inverse temperature β goes from zero to ten in steps of one and from ten to fifty in steps of five.

FIG. 4. Visualization of the temperature dependence (β increasing from zero to ∞from green to red) of the abso- lute value of the first four coefficients c(sc) 2n (β) of the classical complexity early-time series from the semiclassical partition function of DSSYK, normalized by c(sc) 2 (β) and rescaled by (sin θ)2−2n for visual clarity (dashed). They correspond to n = {1, 2, 3, 4} from top to bottom. The first four early-time coefficients of Schwarzian complexity (solid blue) are repro- duced at β →∞, and the first four early-time coefficients of Lβ=0 = 2 log cosh t/2 (solid magenta) at β →0.

FIG. 5. First 100 Lanczos coefficients an(β) in (a) and bn(β) in (b) for Krylov spread complexity of finite temperature TFD state in CFT2. The shaded bands indicate c = 101 (yellow), c = 106 (purple) and c = 1011 (blue). The numerics were carried out at three inverse temperatures β = 1 (green), β = 10−1/2 (orange) and β = 101/2 (red), respectively as indicated by the color of the data points.
